Is failure to thrive a diagnosis?
No. It is a sign of inadequate weight gain, and its cause must be found.
How is failure to thrive defined?
A weight-for-age below −2 standard deviations on repeated measurements, a weight that crosses two major centile lines downwards, or a weight-for-length below −2 standard deviations.
What is the commonest cause of failure to thrive?
Is breastfeeding a cause of failure to thrive?
No. This is the classic "all EXCEPT" answer.
Which feeding errors cause failure to thrive in infants?
Poor breastfeeding technique and over-diluted formula; also late or poor complementary feeding.
Name causes of failure to thrive due to increased needs.
Congenital heart disease with heart failure, tuberculosis, HIV infection, kala-azar, chronic lung disease and hyperthyroidism.
Which renal disease causes failure to thrive with polyuria and rickets?
What are the signs of non-organic failure to thrive?
An occipital bald patch, poor hygiene, avoidance of eye contact, delayed milestones, and rapid weight gain when the child is fed adequately.
An underweight infant gains weight quickly in hospital. What is the diagnosis?
What provides the basis of the diagnosis in failure to thrive?
What are the first-line investigations in failure to thrive?
Complete blood count, urine analysis and culture, stool for parasites and reducing substances, electrolytes, liver function tests and thyroid function tests.
Which test is used to screen for coeliac disease?
How many calories are needed for catch-up growth in failure to thrive?
About 150 kcal/kg/day, calculated on the expected weight. A normal infant needs 100–120 kcal/kg/day.
What are the indications to admit a child with failure to thrive?
Complicated severe acute malnutrition, suspected abuse or neglect, failure of outpatient care, or the need to observe feeding.
According to IMCI, in which children should feeding be assessed?
In children under 2 years, and in any child with anaemia or moderate acute malnutrition.
A height below −2 standard deviations (the 3rd centile) for age and sex.
What height velocity is abnormal before puberty?
A height velocity below 4 cm per year.
What are the commonest causes of short stature?
Normal variants: familial short stature and constitutional delay of growth.
In familial short stature, what are the bone age and the timing of puberty?
The bone age equals the actual age, and puberty starts at a normal age.
In constitutional delay of growth, what are the bone age, puberty and final height?
The bone age is delayed, puberty is delayed, and the final height is normal.
Does acute renal failure cause short stature?
No. Only chronic kidney disease does.
Name causes of disproportionate short stature with short limbs.
What are the causes of short stature with a short trunk?
The mucopolysaccharidoses (such as Morquio syndrome) and disease of the spine.
What are the causes of a child who is short and overweight for height?
Hypothyroidism, growth hormone deficiency, and Cushing syndrome or steroid treatment.
What are the causes of a child who is short and thin?
Malnutrition, coeliac disease, chronic kidney disease, renal tubular acidosis, congenital heart disease, cystic fibrosis and emotional deprivation.
An overweight child has failed to grow and has a delayed bone age. What is the likely cause?
What is the birth size in congenital growth hormone deficiency?
Normal. Growth slows after infancy, because growth hormone has little effect before birth.
What are the neonatal clues to hypopituitarism?
What does a child with growth hormone deficiency look like?
Proportionate short stature, chubby build, an immature doll-like face, a high-pitched voice and a delayed bone age.
Which tumour causes growth hormone deficiency with loss of the visual fields?
How is growth hormone deficiency confirmed?
A low IGF-1 and two growth hormone stimulation tests with a low peak (below 10 ng/mL), followed by an MRI of the pituitary.
A short child has a high growth hormone level and a low IGF-1. What is the diagnosis?
What is the first investigation in a short child?
Bone age: an X-ray of the left hand and wrist.
Which test must be done in every short girl without an obvious cause?
A karyotype, to exclude Turner syndrome.
Why is thyroid function checked before growth hormone testing?
Hypothyroidism lowers growth hormone secretion and gives a falsely low result.
What are the indications for growth hormone therapy?
Growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease, Prader–Willi syndrome, and children born small for gestational age without catch-up growth.
How is constitutional delay of growth treated?
With reassurance. A short course of sex steroid is given if puberty is very late or the child is distressed.
